chunks: Saad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from Khalid ibn Mad al-Qalanisi, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: Regarding the man who catches up with the Imam in the funeral prayer, [catching] one or two takbirs, he said: 'He completes the takbirs while walking with them. If he does not catch the takbir, he says takbir at the grave. If he catches them and they have already buried [the deceased], he says takbir over the grave.'
ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they join the funeral prayer late and miss the Imam's takbirs?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the procedural flexibility for latecomers in the funeral prayer, emphasizing the Imam's role in maintaining congregational unity. It distinguishes between joining during the standing takbirs versus the burial phase, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of adapting ritual actions to the specific stage of the Imam's performance. This ruling underscores the practical application of *ijtihad* in ensuring the validity of individual participation even when missing the full sequence.
